raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-M3 sparse prefill on ROCm currently processes each selected KV block as one full `BLOCK_SIZE_K` tile in the Triton kernel. For the 128-token sparse KV block shape used by MiniMax-M3, that creates a larger dot-product tile than needed for efficient MFMA scheduling and increases register/shared-memory pressure in the prefill kernel.

This PR tunes the sparse prefill kernel so each selected KV block is processed through smaller K sub-tiles while preserving the same online softmax accumulation across the whole sparse block list.

## Modifications

- Add a `SUB_K` compile-time parameter to the MiniMax sparse prefill Triton kernel.
- Split each selected `BLOCK_SIZE_K` KV block into `SUB_K` chunks for the QK and PV dot products.
- Keep the existing online softmax state (`m_i`, `lse_i`, and `acc_o`) across sub-tiles so the output remains mathematically equivalent to processing the full selected KV block at once.
- Use a single CDNA-tuned autotune candidate for this kernel path: `num_warps=1`, `num_stages=1`.
- Pass `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16` and `kpack=2` to guide Triton codegen for the sub-tiled dot products.

## Accuracy Tests

This change preserves the existing sparse attention computation order at the selected-block level and updates only the internal K tiling within each selected block.

Static validation:

```bash
python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/minimax_sparse/prefill/topk_sparse.py
```

GSM8K full set, 1319 examples, `sgl-eval run gsm8k --thinking --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 4096 --num-threads 64`.

Server path: MiniMax-M3 MXFP8, `--tp-size 8`, `--quantization mxfp8`, `--attention-backend triton`, `--moe-runner-backend triton`, and `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`.

| Model/config | Score | Stop rate | Truncated rate | Error rate | Latency | Output tok/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MiniMax-M3 MXFP8, Triton MoE, FSE off | 96.29% | 99.17% | 0.83% | 0.00% | 369.7s | 1180 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Random serving benchmark, 640 prompts, `--random-input-len 8192`, `--random-output-len 1024`, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, `--max-concurrency 64`, `--request-rate inf`, `--warmup-requests 128`, and `--seed 2026`.

Both runs used the same server path: MiniMax-M3 MXFP8, `--tp-size 8`, `--quantization mxfp8`, `--attention-backend triton`, `--moe-runner-backend triton`, and `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`. The baseline is the parent commit before this PR; the PR row enables `SUB_K=64` selected-block sub-tiling.

| Sparse prefill kernel | Successful requests | Duration | Req/s | Input tok/s | Output tok/s | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Parent full-K selected-block tile | 640 | 596.44s | 1.070 | 8790.23 | 1098.78 | 9889.01 | 12277.61 ms | 46.29 ms |
| PR `SUB_K=64` selected-block sub-tiles | 640 | 560.19s | 1.142 | 9359.09 | 1169.89 | 10528.97 | 10491.95 ms | 44.49 ms |
| Delta | - | -6.08% | +6.73% | +6.47% | +6.47% | +6.47% | -14.54% | -3.89% |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
